questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Madagascar?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Madagascar article.

questions.proof: It is off of the East coast of Africa and its capital is Antananarivo.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Madagascar?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Madagascar on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Human history” part of the Madagascar article.

questions.proof: France took over the city of Antananarivo in 1895, and added Madagascar as a colony two years later.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Madagascar?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Madagascar article.

questions.proof: The official languages of Madagascar are Malagasy and French.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Madagascar broke away from _____ and moved closer to Africa.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “away”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Madagascar article, under the heading “Pre-human history”.

questions.proof: When this broke up, Madagascar was attached to what is now the Indian subcontinent.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In regard to being a member of the African Union: As of October _____, its membership has been suspended.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Madagascar article, under the heading “Since independence”.

questions.proof: In regard to being a member of the African Union: As of October 2025, its membership has been suspended.
